mcqs.q: What technique did the study use to obtain expert agreement on welfare-measure weightings?
mcqs.e: Two Delphi procedures were used to build expert consensus on the welfare-score weightings.

mcqs.q: Which type of measure reached consensus faster?
mcqs.e: Animal-based measures achieved consensus more quickly than resource-based measures.

mcqs.q: What does the resulting scoring system produce?
o: A single overall welfare score allowing comparison between shelters
A pass/fail rating with no number
mcqs.e: The study delivered one overall welfare score usable to compare welfare standards across shelters.

mcqs.q: What was the relationship between welfare score and repetitive behaviors in dogs?
mcqs.e: A negative correlation (r=-0.35) showed that lower welfare scores accompanied more repetitive behaviors.

mcqs.q: Compared with healthy dogs, dogs showing repetitive behaviors had welfare scores that were:
mcqs.e: Mean welfare score was 11.6 in affected dogs versus 14.4 in healthy dogs (p<0.001).

mcqs.q: What hypothesis did the findings support?
o: Repetitive behaviors may be linked to poor living conditions
Repetitive behaviors occur only in farm animals
mcqs.e: Results supported that poor living conditions are associated with canine repetitive behaviors.

mcqs.q: Which factors most influenced adopters' decisions in Slovak shelters?
mcqs.e: Age and body weight were the most important factors for early adoption.

mcqs.q: What effect did coat length, color, and sex have on early adoption?
mcqs.e: Coat length, color, and sex had no effect on early adoption.

mcqs.q: How was behavior ranked as an adoption criterion?
o: Important but not the most important
mcqs.e: Behavior mattered during interaction but was not the most important decision criterion.

mcqs.q: Which algorithm performed best for predicting length of stay?
mcqs.e: Gradient boosting had the highest precision, recall, and F1 score.

mcqs.q: Which were found to be important predictor variables?
mcqs.e: Age (puppy/super senior), multicolor coat, and large/small size were key predictors.

mcqs.q: What is the proposed two-phase tool's intended use?
o: Predict and minimize length of stay and euthanization
mcqs.e: The tool aims to reduce length of stay and euthanasia by optimizing shelter allocation.

mcqs.q: What did the study conclude about phenotypic characteristics of dogs?
o: They predict a dog's hazard for euthanasia
mcqs.e: Phenotypic traits were predictive of a dog's hazard for euthanasia versus live release.

mcqs.q: Which factors were significantly associated with euthanasia hazard?
mcqs.e: Age group and skull type were both significantly associated with euthanasia (p<0.0001).

mcqs.q: What statistical model was used?
mcqs.e: A Cox proportional hazard model with a shelter random effect was developed.

mcqs.q: What RTO rate did microchipped at-large adult strays have versus non-microchipped ones?
mcqs.e: Microchipped adult strays had a 71% RTO rate compared with 39% without a microchip.

mcqs.q: How far did most RTOed strays travel from home?
mcqs.e: 70% of RTOed strays traveled at most 1 mile from home.

mcqs.q: What was a practical impact of the tool's findings?
o: Changed stray hold time and targeted microchip programs
mcqs.e: Findings affected the shelter's stray hold time and highlighted target areas for microchip programs.

journal: Journal of Applied Animal Welfare Science

mcqs.q: How did rural pet ownership compare with urban communities?
o: Higher overall pet-keeping and dog ownership
mcqs.e: Rural communities had higher overall pet-keeping and dog ownership than urban ones.

mcqs.q: How did cat ownership rates compare across the four sites?
mcqs.e: Cat ownership was similar across all four sites, averaging 19.4%.

mcqs.q: How did community-specific rates compare with AVMA formula predictions?
o: Differed significantly, though the aggregate matched AVMA
mcqs.e: Community rates differed (p<.0001) from AVMA predictions, yet the aggregate matched the AVMA figure.

journal: Journal of Applied Animal Welfare Science

mcqs.q: What did organizations identify as common reasons for dog relinquishment?
o: Lack of affordable veterinary/behavioral services and pet-friendly housing
mcqs.e: Lack of affordable vet/behavioral services and pet-friendly housing were cited as common reasons.

mcqs.q: Why did organizations discontinue or fail to offer desired programs?
o: Lack of staff and other resources
mcqs.e: Programs were discontinued or unoffered due to lack of staff and resources.

mcqs.q: What did the authors recommend?
o: Strategically develop community-specific programs and partner with vet/behavior professionals
mcqs.e: Authors urged strategically tailored community programs and partnerships with veterinary and behavior professions.

mcqs.q: What did the survey conclude about pandemic fostering?
o: Fostering increased but the impact is likely ephemeral
mcqs.e: Fostering increased during the pandemic, but the effect is likely temporary.

mcqs.q: Which group notably increased fostering?
o: Those unable to work from home
mcqs.e: Increases were particularly seen among volunteers working from home.

mcqs.q: How might organizations retain foster volunteers, per the study?
o: Emotional support directed at the human
mcqs.e: Support, particularly emotional support for the human, may help retain foster volunteers.

mcqs.q: What method was used to predict cat outcomes?
mcqs.e: Structural equation modeling tested four hypotheses on cat outcomes.

mcqs.q: What did the global model indicate about predictors of cat outcomes?
mcqs.e: Multiple interconnected factors, including pre-shelter influences, predict cat outcomes.

mcqs.q: What did the study emphasize incorporating to understand cat outcomes?
mcqs.e: It highlighted the importance of factors occurring outside the shelter.

mcqs.q: How did being a community member with no prior shelter relationship relate to adoption of the fostered dog?
o: Over 4 times more likely to adopt
mcqs.e: New community foster caregivers were over four times more likely to adopt their fostered dog.

mcqs.q: How did shelter resource level relate to foster recruitment?
o: Low-resource shelters recruited new community members most
High-resource shelters more often recruited new community members
mcqs.e: High-resource shelters more often recruited new community members, while low-resource relied on existing relationships.

mcqs.q: What happened to foster utilization over the early pandemic months?
o: Increased March-April then returned to initial levels by June 2020
mcqs.e: Utilization rose from March to April, then returned to initial pandemic levels by June 2020.

mcqs.q: What perception does this review challenge?
o: That behavioral incompatibilities strongly drive relinquishment
mcqs.e: It challenges the belief that behavioral incompatibilities are a major driver of relinquishment.

mcqs.q: What proportion of adopted dogs are returned for behavioral reasons?
mcqs.e: Only about 6-9% of adopted dogs are returned for behavioral reasons.

mcqs.q: What did the authors say about delaying adoption for behavior evaluation/modification?
o: It extends shelter stress, reduces capacity, and consumes staff time
mcqs.e: Delays prolong exposure to shelter stress, reduce capacity, and consume scarce staff time.
